💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: gate the ack-stats fragment on `ackIdle(out)` in the counted line too**

A >=IMPORTANT-only replay (zero below-threshold machine threads, `ackIdle` true) now
appends an idle fragment to the outcome line:

```
…resolved 1, resolve failures 0, ack failures 0; suggestion/nit machine thread(s)
ack-resolved without a fix (wontfix) 0, resolve failures 0, ack-reply failures 0;
0 open human thread(s)…
```

`cleanOutcomeLine` already handles this — it keeps the pure gh-1353 wording when
`ackIdle(out)` is true. `countedOutcomeLine` embeds `ackStatsLine(out)` unconditionally,
so a gh-1353-only replay's log line changes shape for no information. Symmetric form:

```js
', ack failures ' + out.ackFailures + '; ' +
(ackIdle(out) ? '' : ackStatsLine(out) + '; ') + out.human.length +
```

Optional polish — the lines are informational only (no machine parser consumes them,
verified by grep), so behavior is unaffected either way.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: dedupe the twin `backstopBridgeMocks` builders into `_fixtures/`**

`js/unit-tests/test_mergeBot.js` and `js/unit-tests/test_mergeTrigger.js` carry
near-identical copies of `backstopBridgeMocks`, and this PR had to extend both copies
with the exact same `resolveFailIds` branch — the classic parallel-edit cost of
duplicated fixtures (miss one copy and the two suites silently diverge in failure
injection capability).

The repo already has a shared-fixture pattern: `js/unit-tests/_fixtures/releaseArtefactsMock.js`
is loaded via `loadModule('js/unit-tests/_fixtures/…', makeRequire({}, {}), {})` in
multiple suites. Extracting the builder there (e.g. `_fixtures/backstopBridgeMocks.js`,
taking `(opts, calls)` and returning the mock bag) ends the parallel edits — and doing
it together with the resolve-fail extraction from the blocking thread drops both copies
below the CRAP ratchet in one move.

The two copies do differ today (mergeBot's also mocks `github_search_issues` for
`calls.debtSearches`) — parameterize that one difference rather than merging blindly.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: document the `none`-severity fallthrough onto the wontfix ack path**

The ack path covers everything below rank(IMPORTANT) — including a machine thread whose
body carries **no recognizable severity marker**. `reviewVerdicts.threadSeverity`
returns `'none'` for it, and `findingRegistry.severityClassOf` falls back to
`'SUGGESTION'` (`findingRegistry.js:225` — `'NIT'` also maps through the fallback, so
it lands here deliberately). Net behavior: a marker-less machine-owned thread is now
auto-resolved at merge time with a public
`wontfix: below gating threshold — epic invariant (gh-1370)` ack — under gh-1353 it was
left untouched ("the triage path's business").

Confirm this is intended. For what it's worth, the alternative is a deadlock: holding
the merge on an unresolvable classification would never converge, so ack-path is the
only terminal outcome for such threads — but that reasoning (and the `'none' → ack`
fallthrough) deserves one line in the `classifyThreads` doc comment so a later audit
reading the digest/ack trail understands why a marker-less thread closed as `wontfix`
rather than being a misclassification.
